Subject: E-sign vendor consolidation: scope, timeline & vendor asks

Team —

Quick context: as part of our Q3 cost and security review I think it makes sense to evaluate consolidating our two primary e-signing paths (Ironclad for contract authoring + DocuSign for external envelopes) into a single contract/operational model. The goal is to reduce per-envelope spend, simplify SSO/audit retention, and centralize API keys for the platform.

High-level asks I want us to align on before we go to vendors:
- Target outcome: single enterprise agreement (or a clear interoperability plan) that covers templates, API usage, audit logging, and SSO.
- Timeline: vendor responses by 6/18, exec decision by 7/2, migration plan drafted by 7/16.
- Key evaluation criteria: pricing (per-envelope vs committed), security evidence (SOC2 + pen test reports), retention & eDiscovery features, API rate limits, and migration effort (template & history port).

Attached is a short RFP draft I pulled together (Redwood_Esign_RFP.pdf). Please review and add any must-have items.

Next steps: Markus, can you flag any legal constraints or standard terms that would block consolidation? Laura, can you confirm whether there are regulatory retention windows we need to preserve (we have a few FinServ PoCs). Marissa/Rishi, can you run cost scenario modeling for: 1) keep both vendors, 2) consolidate to Ironclad, 3) consolidate to DocuSign. I can consolidate vendor replies and manage scheduling.

Thanks —
Naomi
Naomi Feldman

Subject: Re: E-sign vendor consolidation: scope, timeline & vendor asks

Naomi —

High level: I support exploring consolidation but want to call out a few gating legal/infosec items before we commit vendor-side:

1) Data residency / export controls: any migration plan must preserve chain-of-custody for executed agreements. If we plan to export historical signed PDFs to a new provider we need a signed statement around custody and access logs.

2) Indemnity & liability caps: when we consolidate e-signing as a critical path for contracts, we should ensure vendor indemnities and SLA credits align with our revenue scale. Expect us to push for a $5M cap or a tiered cap tied to annual run-rate.

3) Evidence (SOC2/reporting): we need recent SOC2 Type II and a copy of the pen test summary. For DocuSign specifically, check their eDiscovery and envelope-retention controls — we may have to keep a cold copy of certain FinServ documents for 7 years.

4) Standard redlines: I'll prepare a checklist of redlines (data processing addendum, subprocessor list, termination/exit assistance, escrow) by EOD Friday (6/12).

If we decide to run both vendors in parallel during migration, include an option in the RFP for dual-running and data sync support.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Legal — Contracts & Compliance

Thanks for the note and for sharing the RFP. Quick responses below and attached our starter pricing workbook (ironclad-enterprise-pricing.xlsx).

- Pricing: we have committed-envelope tiers at 100k/250k/500k annual volumes. We can offer a migration credit equivalent to 20% of first-year committed spend if you sign a 36-month agreement. Per-envelope pricing + API calls bundled.
- Migration: Ironclad Professional Services supports template import and can import bulk signed PDFs into our vault. We recommend a short dual-run period (2–4 weeks) and we provide a sync tool for template parity.
- Security: attached SOC2 Type II and a redacted pentest summary. We can add a clause for exit assistance & custody verification in the MSA; sample language attached.
- Throughput: our platform supports up to ~1,500 envelope creation calls/min on enterprise nodes; we'll work with your infra team on burst patterns.

We can hop on a call Mon/Tue next week (6/15–6/16). Proposed attendees: product infra + legal.
